newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Cook, Albright deliver joint message on Hong Kong.
newsitem.headline: Cook, Albright deliver joint message on Hong Kong.

text.p: With the Hong Kong handover hours away, the United States and Britain on Monday delivered a strong joint message to China to maintain the territory's freedoms as it comes under Beijing's control.

"We are both confident that Hong Kong can have a prosperous future and a free future if the terms of the (1984 Sino-British) Joint Declaration are adhered to," said British Foreign Secretary Robin Cook after talks on the royal yacht Britannia with U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright.

In particular, Cook said there was concern that an elected Hong Kong legislature will be disbanded at midnight to be replaced with a Beijing-appointed body. The two officials also repeated calls for new elections "as soon as possible."

Albright, standing at dockside with Cook for a joint news conference, said: "I join the foreign secretary in expressing our expectation that China will keep its word and maintain Hong Kong's autonomy and way of life for decades to come."
They repeated criticism of Beijing's decision to send 4,000 Chinese troops into the territory hours after Hong Kong reverts at midnight to Chinese control after 156 years of British rule.

Cook stressed the importance that Chinese troops not be seen on the streets of Hong Kong "where they have no right" under the terms of the joint declaration, under which Britain and China set terms for the transition of power.
